<Rep. Robert C. "Bobby" Scott, Rep. Joe Courtney, Rep. Frederica S. Wilson, Rep. Suzanne Bonamici, Rep. Mark DeSaulnier, Rep. Jahana Hayes, Rep. Ilhan Omar, Rep. Summer L. Lee, Rep. Adelita S. Grijalva>: Ensuring the integrity of the CCDBG program is certainly essential, but removing Secretarial discretion to impose sanctions would threaten to detract from the main purpose of the program--to provide for families in need of child care payment assistance. Based on the reaction to unproven cases of fraud we have seen from the Trump administration and Committee Majority,\47\ it is reasonable to ask: what levels of noncompliance will trigger the requirement that the Secretary impose draconian sanctions? Would one proven case of fraud that a state did not handle in the manner the Secretary demanded endanger a whole state from losing its funds? Importantly, H.R. 7726 covers sanctions not just for fraud but with a failure of state to ``comply substantially'' with its state plan or the CCDBG Act.\48\ Could a widespread technical violation by the state with no malicious intent trigger sanctions from a capricious Secretary? By leaving the HHS Secretary no discretion to impose additional sanctions in instances of noncompliance, H.R. 7726 turns every such instance into one that requires extreme penalties. This increases the chances a state will be sanctioned, which could result in taking funding and resources away from families who need support in affording child care.
\47\See supra text accompanying notes 16-24.
\48\42 U.S.C. Sec. 9858g(b)(2)(A).
DEMOCRATIC AMENDMENTS OFFERED DURING MARKUP OF H.R. 7726
Ranking Member Scott offered an amendment to require HHS to work with the Department of Homeland Security to prevent immigration enforcement at day care centers. The purpose of the amendment is to ensure that all children and families, regardless of their immigration status, can receive safe, quality child care by requiring the Secretary of HHS to enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security that prevents enforcement actions by Immigration and Enforcement and Customs and Border protection in and near child care centers. Since the start of the Trump Administration, we have seen unprecedented immigration enforcement actions at and near places that were previously understood to be off-limits, like schools and child care centers.\49\ The Trump Administration's immigration raids near child care centers have traumatized children and communities and added heavy burdens on teachers and caregivers.\50\ If we want to create a safe environment for all children and families, we should not be allowing masked, armed federal agents to enter these spaces. Although the amendment was supported by a bipartisan group of Members--specifically all Democrats as well as Rep. Kevin Kiley (I-CA)\51\--the majority of Committee Republicans rejected the amendment. Therefore, the amendment failed.
\49\See e.g., Letter from 71 House Members to The Honorable Linda McMahon, Secretary, U.S. Dep't of Educ. (Feb. 17, 2026), https:// democrats-edworkforce.house.gov/imo/media/doc/scott_bonamici_follow-up_letter_to_ed_on_immigration_policies_k12_impact.pdf.
\50\See e.g., Samie Solina, Local child care centers report ICE detentions, federal visits amid rising concerns, KARE11 Minneapolis St. Paul (Jan. 13, 2026) https://www.kare11.com/article/news/politics/ immigration-news/local-child-care-centers-report-ice-detentions-federal-visits/89-2dc1ce9e-8b8a-4964-81c0-b52715e98b8e.
\51\At the time of this markup, Rep. Kiley was a Republican but has since changed his affiliation to Independent.
CONCLUSION
While it is important to address any instance of fraud with federal funds designed to support child care programs, this bill would hurt the program more than it would help. It is also important to note that there has been no evidence of the Majority's allegations of widespread fraud. For the reasons stated above, Committee Democrats unanimously opposed H.R. 7726 when the Committee on Education and Workforce considered it on March 5, 2026. We urge the House of Representatives to do the same.
Robert C. ``Bobby'' Scott,
Ranking Member.
Joe Courtney,
Frederica Wilson,
Suzanne Bonamici,
Mark DeSaulnier,
Jahana Hayes,
Ilhan Omar,
Summer Lee,
Adelita Grijalva,
Members of Congress.
